title: I Took the Nail-Salon Chair Timer to the Stylist Who Booked Over Me

parts.text: I sat in chair 4 at 2:00 p.m. with a confirmation text and wet primer already on my thumbs. Mara looked at the iPad and said a bride had taken the slot. I was twenty-six, dental assistant on my lunch, holding a paper smock. The salon timer on the mirror said 60 MINUTES FROM SEATED. I had been seated. Mara started the bride two chairs over and told me to wait by the dryer. I photographed the timer, the confirmation, and the empty chair 4. Then I asked the owner, who was folding towels, whether seated meant seated. She winced. The bride's music was already playing. At 2:11 Mara's own next client arrived and the iPad pinged double-book.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The iPad just pinged a double-book while I still have primer on my thumbs.

social.video_title: She seated me, then seated a bride in my hour — Part 1/2
social.description: Lunch break, wet primer, a timer on the mirror. The iPad knew. Would you have washed it off?

parts.text: The owner honored the timer. Mara finished the bride's left hand at a different station and I got chair 4 back with eight minutes of my lunch remaining plus the owner's apology gel. I paid for what I received. Mara's review reply said miscommunication. The confirmation screenshot is not a dialect. The salon added a seated lock on the iPad. I book Mara only if the lock shows green. Primer is a contract. Lunch is not a waiting room.

social.video_title: Seated lock is now a real button — Part 2/2
social.description: Chair 4, apology gel, an iPad that learned. Was a bride a confirmation text?
